name: Tie Rods
description: Inner tie rods (ball joint threaded onto the rack bar), outer tie rod ends (tapered stud into the knuckle steering arm) and the jam nuts that lock toe.

components.name: Inner tie rod
components.description: Axial ball joint threaded onto the end of the rack bar, protected by the rack boot. Its threaded outer end receives the outer tie rod end; turning it changes toe. On lowered cars the inner joint can bind at full bump/lock - check articulation (SPL notes binding can bend/break inner tie rods on heavily lowered cars).
components.location: From rack end approx (x -0.13, y 0.26, z +/-0.38) outward to approx z +/-0.60.

raceOptions.name: OE inner with SPL TRE CAM6 outer assembly
raceOptions.notes: SPL bump-steer tie rod ends thread onto the OE inner tie rod (see steering.bump-steer).

hardware.item: Inner tie rod to rack (threaded joint)
hardware.spec: Inner tie rod socket thread onto rack bar
hardware.torqueSequence: Hold rack bar to avoid loading pinion teeth
hardware.threadlocker: Per GM SI (typically threadlocker on rack thread)
hardware.notes: Value from a GM SI-derived listing; another secondary source lists 50 ft-lb - verify.

installNotes: Count turns when removing to preserve approximate toe.
Stake/lock per GM procedure if applicable.
inspection: Check axial play by gripping through boot (wheels on ground, rock steering).

modelRef.features: Axial ball socket on the rack end, straight rod, threaded end (item 7)

components.name: Outer tie rod end
components.description: Ball joint with a tapered stud that fits the knuckle steering arm and threads onto the inner tie rod. Its stud height relative to the lower links governs bump steer - the race replacement is an adjustable-height rod-end assembly (SPL TRE CAM6).
components.location: Steering arm at front of knuckle, approx (x -0.12, y 0.25, z +/-0.68).

raceOptions.name: SPL Parts TRE CAM6 bumpsteer-adjustable tie rod ends

hardware.item: Outer tie rod end stud nut (to knuckle)
hardware.torqueSequence: 35 N·m first pass + final angle per GM SI (angle not in available source). Secondary source lists 42 ft-lb.
hardware.notes: GM SI-derived listing also shows a 'steering knuckle nut' 40 N·m first pass - confirm which applies in GM SI. [2026-10 check] No Gen 6 or Alpha source with the final angle was found. Zeta cars (Chevy SS, G8) use 18 lb-ft + 115–125°, but that platform differs and its value should not be used here. The first pass stays per TightTorque.

installNotes: Clean taper dry; hold stud with hex key if it spins.
inspection: Check for play and boot condition.

modelRef.features: Forged cranked tie-rod end with ball stud pointing up into the knuckle steering arm (item 4)

components.name: Tie rod jam nut
components.description: Lock nut that clamps the outer tie rod end to the inner tie rod after toe is set.
components.location: Between inner tie rod and outer tie rod end, approx z +/-0.61.

hardware.spec: Jam nut on inner tie rod thread (approx M14-M16 fine thread; verify)
hardware.notes: Typical GM value range; not verified for Gen 6 - check SI.

installNotes: Hold the outer tie rod end flat while tightening so the ball stud is centered in its travel.

modelRef.features: Jam nut on the inner tie-rod thread (item 8)
